We need to propose a retrosynthesis route up to 3 steps, leaves must be commercially available, total price <=9999. Need to find templates. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with proper list. We need to break the target into simpler fragments. The target: a sulfonamide linking a tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) to a phenyl sulfonyl attached to a phenyl with a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So maybe disconnections: 1) disconnection of sulfonamide bond (S-N). 2) disconnection of amide bond (C=O-N). 3) maybe disconnection of the C=C double bond (retro-aldol? but maybe not needed). Aim for 3 steps.

We can propose route: Step1: Form sulfonamide between p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) and an aniline bearing the rest of molecule (the phenyl with the α,β-unsaturated amide). Actually target has sulfonyl attached to phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2) which is attached to sulfonyl group (S(=O)(=O)). The sulfonyl is attached to the aniline (NS(=O)(=O)Ar). So we could start from p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The sulfonyl group is attached to the first phenyl (c1ccc...). Actually SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1. So we have a tolyl (methyl phenyl) attached via N to sulfonyl attached to second phenyl (c2...). So the sulfonyl is attached to the second phenyl, not the first. So the sulfonamide is between the first aniline (p-toluidine) and the sulfonyl attached to second phenyl. So we could make sulfonamide by reacting p-toluidine with a sulfonyl chloride derived from the second phenyl (i.e., 4-(... )-benzenesulfonyl chloride). That second phenyl has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N (trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline). So we could make that phenyl sulfonyl chloride from that phenyl with side chain, perhaps via chlorosulfonation of that phenyl (but that may be step). Alternatively, we could form the amide later.

Maybe better: Disconnection of amide: break C(=O)-N to give an acid (or acid chloride) and an aniline (c3ccccc3N). The side chain is C=O attached to N-aryl (aniline). So we could have 4-(... )-benzoic acid (or acid chloride) reacting with aniline to give amide. The side chain also includes a trans-alkene attached to phenyl. That could be formed via Heck coupling or Wittig.

Simplify: Step1: Form amide between 4-(trans-phenyl-CH=CH-COOH) (or acid chloride) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). That yields the side chain attached to phenyl (c2...). Then step2: sulfonylate that phenyl with sulfonyl chloride derived from p-toluidine? Actually we need sulfonamide linking p-toluidine to that phenyl sulfonyl. So we could react p-toluidine with the sulfonyl chloride of the phenyl (which already has the amide side chain). So step2: sulfonyl chloride formation from phenyl (maybe via chlorosulfonation) then sulfonamide formation with p-toluidine. That's 2 steps after making the phenyl sulfonyl chloride (which may be considered a reagent, maybe commercially available? 4-(trans-... )-benzenesulfonyl chloride maybe not common). Could we instead start from p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) and the aniline (the phenyl with side chain) to form sulfonamide? That would attach the sulfonyl to the aniline (the phenyl with side chain) and the N would be attached to the sulfonyl, but the N would be part of the phenyl? Wait TsCl is p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). Reacting with aniline (the phenyl with side chain) would give N-sulfonyl aniline (i.e., the sulfonyl attached to the aniline nitrogen). That would produce the target where the sulfonyl phenyl is p-tolyl, not the other phenyl. But target has sulfonyl phenyl being the second phenyl (c2...), not p-tolyl. So we need sulfonyl phenyl = phenyl with side chain. So we need sulfonyl chloride of that phenyl. Might not be commercially available.

Alternative route: Form sulfonamide first between p-toluidine and a simple sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) to give N-(p-tolyl)sulfonamide attached to p-tolyl? Not correct.

Maybe we can reverse: The sulfonyl phenyl could be introduced via a sulfonylation of the p-toluidine using a sulfonyl chloride derived from the phenyl with side chain. If that sulfonyl chloride is not commercially available, we could generate it from the phenyl sulfonic acid (which could be made via sulfonation of the phenyl). Sulfonation of aromatic rings is cheap reagents (e.g., fuming sulfuric acid). Could be considered a step.

Given constraints, we can propose 3 steps: 1) Synthesize the phenyl sulfonyl chloride (via sulfonation of the phenyl with side chain, then chlorination). 2) Form sulfonamide with p-toluidine. 3) Form amide via coupling of the side chain acid (or acid chloride) with aniline? Wait the side chain is already attached to the phenyl before sulfonylation? The side chain is attached to the phenyl (c2...). So we need to have that phenyl bearing the side chain before sulfonyl chloride formation. So step1: Build the phenyl with side chain (i.e., 4-(trans-... )-aniline? Actually the phenyl with side chain also has the sulfonyl group attached later. So we could first make the phenyl with side chain as a benzoic acid derivative, then sulfonylate.

Simplify: Use commercially available 4-aminobenzoic acid (PABA) maybe? But side chain is trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. That's a cinnamoyl anilide attached to phenyl. Could be made via coupling of trans-cinnamic acid with aniline. Then we need to attach sulfonyl group to the phenyl ring (para position). Could use sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) to sulfonylate the aniline? Not.

Maybe we can propose a convergent route: Step1: Prepare the amide side chain: trans-cinnamic acid + 4-aminophenyl (c3ccccc3N) yields trans-cinnamoyl aniline (C=O-NH-Ph). That's the side chain attached to phenyl? Actually the side chain is attached to phenyl via the carbonyl: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2. So the phenyl (c2) is attached to carbonyl via the double bond: phenyl-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2. So the phenyl (c2) is the one bearing the alkene and carbonyl. So we need a phenyl with a trans-CH=CH-CO-NH-Ph-NH2 substituent at para position? Actually the SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl (c2) has the side chain at para position (maybe). So we need to attach that side chain to phenyl. That could be done via Heck coupling of a phenyl bromide with trans-ethyl acrylate then convert to acid then amide. Or via Suzuki.

Given time, maybe we can cheat: Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria to find templates that break amide and sulfonamide. Then apply them to get precursors. Then check buyability.

Let's search for templates that break amide (functional_groups_broken = ["amide"]).
